title: VeReMi: A Dataset for Comparable Evaluation of Misbehavior Detection in VANETs
authors: Rens W. van der Heijden, Thomas Lukaseder, Frank Kargl
dataset: VeReMi (original; LuST + modified Veins; 225 simulations = 5 attackers x 3 attacker fractions x 3 densities x 5 repetitions)
attacks: 5 position-falsification attacks: constant (1), constant offset (2), random (4), random offset (8), eventual stop (16). No Sybil attack (ghost vehicles named as future work)
unit: per reception event at the receiving vehicle ('a detection event occurs whenever a message is received')
features: raw BSM fields + receiver GPS; detectors use position / speed / range
model: 4 rule-based plausibility detectors: acceptance range threshold, sudden appearance warning, simple speed check, distance moved verifier (several thresholds each)
split_protocol: no train/test split (no learned model); no official split is defined for later ML users
metrics_result: precision-recall curves + a Gini index of error dispersion across vehicles; few exact numbers in text; main finding: acceptance range threshold and simple speed check are complementary
code: yes - dataset + generation code https://veremi-dataset.github.io/ ; Maat framework https://github.com/vs-uulm/Maat
limitation_gap: Defines no train/val/test split, so every later ML paper invents its own. Authors themselves write 'we caution against using this data (or even our simulation code) as the sole foundation' for evaluating machine-learned models.
relevance_why: The dataset origin; its missing split protocol and the authors' own caution about ML evaluation motivate our split/leak analysis.
verified_via: ar5iv full text of arXiv:1804.06701 fetched (attacks, 225 runs, detectors, metrics, unit, quote); arXiv abstract page; Springer record via search
